description: The `compute-depth` function defines a `memo` hashtable but never uses it to store or retrieve results, leading to redundant recursive graph traversals and potentially exponential complexity on certain graph structures.
suggested_fix: Use `hashtable-ref` to check for existing results and `hashtable-set!` to store computed depths within the `depth` helper function.

description: The `hydrate-cas!` function loads the entire content-addressed store from disk into an in-memory hashtable. This causes unbounded memory growth proportional to the size of the store on disk.
suggested_fix: Implement a cache with an eviction policy (e.g., LRU) or rely on lazy loading from disk instead of pre-loading all blocks.

description: `store-all-blocks` eagerly loads all blocks into memory as a list. Functions like `store-filter` and `store-stats` depend on this, leading to high memory pressure and slow execution on large stores.
suggested_fix: Use a generator or stream-based approach to iterate over blocks lazily without loading the entire set into memory.

description: `count-by-tag` uses an alist and `map` to update counts for every block, resulting in O(N*T) complexity where T is the number of unique tags.
code_snippet: (if existing (map (lambda (pair) (if (eq? (car pair) tag) (cons tag (+ 1 (cdr pair))) pair)) counts) (cons (cons tag 1) counts))
suggested_fix: Use a hashtable for O(N) tag counting instead of an alist with nested mapping.

description: Manual implementation of `list-sort` uses a naive quicksort approach which has O(N^2) worst-case complexity and creates many intermediate list allocations.
code_snippet: (define (list-sort less? lst) ... (append (list-sort less? smaller) (list pivot) (list-sort less? greater)))
suggested_fix: Use Chez Scheme's built-in `list-sort` which is highly optimized.

description: `find-popular` performs a full store scan with individual `fs-fetch` calls (disk I/O) for every block to count inbound references. This is O(N) disk operations per call.
suggested_fix: Implement a persistent index for reference counts or cache the results of the reference scan.

description: `bx-search` performs a linear scan of all blocks, fetching each from disk and performing UTF-8 conversion and string searching on the payload. This is extremely slow for large stores.
suggested_fix: Use the indexing system (e.g., `shell/blocks/block-index.ss`) to perform content-based queries more efficiently.

description: `list-identity-heads` uses a hardcoded list of potential users and checks for file existence for each, which is inefficient and won't scale to many users.
code_snippet: (let ([potential-users '(alice bob charlie dave eve test)]) (filter (lambda (username) (file-exists? (identity-head-path username))) potential-users))
suggested_fix: Use `directory-list` on the `*identity-heads-dir*` to find all actual identity files.

description: `block-compare-many` performs pairwise comparison of all blocks in the provided list, resulting in O(N^2) complexity.
suggested_fix: If N is large, consider more efficient similarity clustering or only comparing against a representative set of blocks.
